Not much. I was able to get a small team to do some digging on motivations in crowd behavior
and with a special focus on sports, but not much turned up, aside from how poorly mapped it is.
The history of football was good to recount, in that in the middle ages whole villages would play
each other and it could turn hostile, but perhaps this actually diffused violence overall if it helped
people settle petty scores and move on, rather for grudges to fester into something more mutually
destructive (thus keeping fit but saving energy for important conflict). Similar things arc seen in
ritualized conflicts in animals, and one wonders how many ways this is woven into common
culture today in social conflicts expressed through the media, etc.
Overall, lots of soft emotional stuff, and probably hard to study from bottom up via complex
motivations and emotions but probably easier to understand via the evolution and design of mass
entertainment and mass media.

Still, there is potential here....
